commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 63 (other made-up textile articles) composition derived its action-incidence flags from exemplar HTS lines belonging to other chapters, so every branch they gate was grounded on provisions outside this chapter and could never fire for a chapter 63 entry.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 60. Read the diff in full; removal of the five derived rules plus the generator-version/summary sentence only.
triage.verifier_justification: The ch63 diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas are `hts_number == "<line>"` for HTS 7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30 and 8541.42.00.10 — lines in chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85 — each carrying proof atoms citing those other chapters' corpus paths inside a chapter 63 composition whose own rate table is keyed on 6301-series lines (`corpus_citation_path: us/statute/hts/6301.10.00.00`) and whose summary states that "Chapter and rate-line routing occur in entry preparation, never through cross-chapter RuleSpec dispatch." Those five identifiers gate roughly fifteen live formulas in this module (the five China §301 list slots, the §232 aluminum branch, the §201 solar zeroing, the §338 Canada-alcohol term, the Brazil IEEPA carve-out and the §122 exemption gate), so before the fix every one of those branches was grounded on provisions outside this chapter and could never be true for an entry that reaches ch63 — exactly "a branch, condition, or value with no basis in the cited source ... including formulas grounded on the wrong provision," which the fix re-grounds by making them caller-supplied incidence inputs. I tested the two competing readings and rejected both: it is not mechanical (five rules with proof atoms are deleted and five identifiers change from locally derived to caller inputs, changing the module's input surface and the resolved value of gating conditions), and it is not a bare enhancement, since the module already emitted `schedule_statutory_stack` for chapter 63 entries with those components summed and the PR frames the exemplar coupling as having "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins." wrong_entity_or_scope is a near miss, but the decisive evidence is the proof atoms citing the wrong chapters' provisions, which the kind list assigns to untraceable_branch.
triage.verifier_notes:
Decisive supporting lines, all verbatim from the diff: the removed rule headers `-- name: entry_is_line_a` .. `entry_is_line_e`, their removed proof atoms `-          corpus_citation_path: us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00` (and 7601.10.30.00 / 9506.62.40.40 / 2203.00.00.30 / 8541.42.00.10), and the added summary sentence "The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification."

Caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1) The repair is PARTIAL in this module. After the commit, ch63 still contains `entry_is_energy_resource` with formula `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"` (post line 1950, proof atoms citing us/statute/hts/7202 and us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00) — i.e. a ferroalloy line used as the chapter 63 proxy for the 9903.01.13 energy/critical-minerals carve-out. The same exemplar grounding therefore survives this commit; only the five entry_is_line_* flags were removed.
2) Stale artifacts remain: `source_verification.corpus_citation_paths` still lists all five exemplar lines (2203.00.00, 7202, 7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 8541.42.00, 9506.62.40 ...) and the unchanged rationale block still says the composition contributes "line selection over the five encoded HTS statistical reporting numbers."
3) Behavior in THIS commit changes only the input surface — the five identifiers go from "necessarily false for any ch63 entry" to caller-supplied; the PR asserts witness-slice equivalence "exact under input mapping," so the observable duty change materializes once entry preparation feeds real membership values (and the PR's later commit re-gates §122 on entry_is_section_122_exempt / entry_is_section_232_covered and adds the steel component — those are not in this module's diff).
4) Corpus dedup: this identical change is applied to all 100 generated chapter modules in commit 2a6bdb01de; ch63 (module index 62) is one instance of a single generator-level defect, not 100 independent defects.
5) A later PR comment notes flags c and e were dropped as valid input slots ("companion tests now feed only the retained exemplar flags (a/b/d)"), which is downstream of this commit.
